name: stable-diffusion.cpp
description: A ggml-based C/C++ diffusion runtime, the image-generation counterpart of llama.cpp. It is a command-line program (`sd-cli`) that writes a PNG, not a server: there is no HTTP API to attach to, so the harness drives it through a command template and measures the process. It is the only lane here that loads GGUF, and it loads the transformer, the text encoder and the VAE as three separate files.

install.notes: There are no published binaries for aarch64 CUDA; build from the tag named by the engine version.

serve.notes: Not a serve command: sd-cli renders one image per invocation and exits, so this is the template the image runner fills per request. The flag names are the ones the project's own Qwen-Image docs use (--diffusion-model, --vae, --llm, -p, -W, -H, --seed, -o, and -r for a reference image, repeated once per reference). `--llm` is a separate file: which text encoder and at which quantization is part of the configuration and belongs in args, because a Q8_0 transformer with a bf16 text encoder is not the same lane as a Q8_0 transformer with a Q8_0 one.

notes: A CLI lane has no queue and no warm process: every image pays the model load unless the build keeps it resident, so load_s is part of the measurement here in a way it is not for a server, and s_per_image without it is the number to compare. versions_available is empty on purpose. A version file has to carry that build's real flags and their real defaults (AGENTS.md), and a wrong default silently merges two configurations into one fingerprint. Nobody has installed this engine for this model yet, so the first run that does reads `--help` on the actual build and adds the version file in the same pull request as its numbers.
